theses.subject: Big Pharma
theses.thesis: Big Pharma is the headline theme, trend-eligible with the highest durability_bar among eligible leaders (0.84), full breadth (1.0), and a confirming trend tag. The absolute-trend gate (the one validated risk-control leg) is supportive here. Crowding (z=1.46) is a size-down caution, not a fade signal, consistent with guardrails against fading the dominant theme.
theses.dissent: Big Pharma is crowded (z=1.46) and headline-positioned, which historically marks attention tops; if breadth begins to roll over while price stays flat, the leadership is decaying and this becomes a dead-money overweight.

falsifier.text: PPH lags the S&P 500 by 3% or more over any rolling 10-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Health Care (Equal-Weight)
theses.thesis: Health Care EW is trend-eligible with strong durability (0.78) and very high breadth (0.917), but it is crowded (z=1.54). It shares the defensive-healthcare leadership of Big Pharma and offers a slightly less headline-concentrated exposure. Crowding cautions against aggressive positioning.
theses.dissent: Extreme crowding (z=1.54) means any mean-reversion in defensive positioning could hit this hard; equal-weight healthcare is not a pure play and may lag if a single mega-cap pharma name dominates

falsifier.text: XLV underperforms SPY by 2% or more over any rolling 10-day period before the check-by date

theses.subject: Defensives
theses.thesis: Defensives (consumer staples + utilities basket) is trend-eligible, durable (0.82), and broad (0.944), but unscorable as a clean single-ETF proxy. It fits the defensive cluster but offers no clean accountability, so conviction is capped.
theses.dissent: Unscorable with a single proxy means this lean cannot be cleanly graded; defensive crowding is extreme across the cluster and a risk-on reversal would hit staples/utilities disproportionately

falsifier.text: A blended XLP/XLU equal-weight basket trails SPY by 2% over any rolling 10-day window before the check-by date
